items.title: The US, with Europe as a second home
items.text: US near a third, Europe's big three up to a tenth

items.title: New mechanics, not strategy's inertia
items.text: Merge games up 9.74 points in a year

items.title: PC and console, run like a small team
items.text: The ceiling is real, so is a 3,070 peak

items.title: Compliance and localization, finished
items.text: Pick your markets, then your gates

notes: Five calls. One: bet on retention, not acquisition. Player numbers at home have peaked, user acquisition abroad is expensive, and the association explains both last year's and this half's overseas growth by the long-term operation of existing titles. The growth is in depth of operation. Two: bet on the US, and run Europe as a second home. Not giving up on Japan, but Japan now has to be won again, product by product. Three: strategy takes half the top-100 money. That makes it the base, and also crowded. Merge games reached 16.22% this half, up 9.74 points year on year, so the top of the chart can still be rewritten by new mechanics. Four: PC and console are a second channel, but budget it like a small team, not like Black Myth. Five: finish compliance and localization properly. Decide where you operate first, then which gates you go through. These are calls, not forecasts. I'm not giving you a number for ten years from now.
